findings.title: Title is too short
findings.detail: The title is too short to describe the page. Search engines may rewrite it, and it wastes the most visible line in results.

fix.summary: Expand the title to 30-60 characters: page topic first, brand last.
steps: Describe what the page offers in plain words.
Append the brand name after a separator.
fix.codeHint: <title>Fast, accessible websites for small teams | Northwind</title>
acceptance: The <title> is 30-60 characters and describes the page topic.

findings.title: Meta description is missing
findings.detail: Without a meta description, search engines pick a snippet from the page, which is often a menu or cookie notice.

fix.summary: Add a meta description of 70-160 characters that summarises the page and invites the click.
steps: Write one or two sentences about what the visitor gets on this page.
Add it to <head>.
fix.codeHint: <meta name="description" content="What this page offers, in one or two sentences.">
acceptance: The page has one <meta name="description"> with 70-160 characters.

findings.title: Page has no main heading (h1)
findings.detail: There's no visible <h1>. Screen reader users and search engines use it to understand what the page is about.

fix.summary: Mark up the main page heading as a single visible <h1>.
steps: Find the largest heading at the top of the page.
Change its element to <h1> (keep the styling with a class).
Make sure no other element on the page is an <h1>.
fix.codeHint: What this page is about
acceptance: The page has exactly one visible <h1> with text.
fix.verify: In DevTools console: `document.querySelectorAll('h1').length === 1`

findings.title: Heading levels skip
findings.detail: Headings jump levels (for example h2 to h4). The outline becomes confusing for screen reader users who navigate by heading.

fix.summary: Use heading levels in order without skipping, and style them with classes rather than picking levels for size.
steps: List headings in order (DevTools or a headings bookmarklet).
Change each skipped level to the next level down from its parent.
Move visual sizing into CSS classes.
acceptance: No heading is more than one level deeper than the heading before it.

findings.title: Heading levels skip
findings.detail: Headings jump levels (for example h2 to h4). The outline becomes confusing for screen reader users who navigate by heading.

fix.summary: Use heading levels in order without skipping, and style them with classes rather than picking levels for size.
steps: List headings in order (DevTools or a headings bookmarklet).
Change each skipped level to the next level down from its parent.
Move visual sizing into CSS classes.
acceptance: No heading is more than one level deeper than the heading before it.

findings.title: No canonical URL
findings.detail: Without a canonical link, URL variants (tracking parameters, trailing slashes) can be indexed as duplicates.

fix.summary: Add a self-referencing canonical link with the absolute, preferred URL.
steps: Add <link rel="canonical"> to <head> with the page's preferred absolute URL.
Generate it per page in your layout or SEO component.
fix.codeHint: <link rel="canonical" href="https://example.com/page">
acceptance: The page has exactly one <link rel="canonical"> with an absolute URL to itself.

findings.title: Social sharing tags are incomplete
findings.detail: Open Graph and Twitter tags control the preview card when the page is shared. Missing tags give a bare link or a random image.

fix.summary: Add og:title, og:description, og:image (1200x630) and twitter:card.
steps: Create a 1200x630 share image.
Add the Open Graph tags and twitter:card to <head>, per page.
fix.codeHint:
<meta property="og:title" content="Page title">
<meta property="og:description" content="One-sentence summary.">
<meta property="og:image" content="https://example.com/og.png">
<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image">
acceptance: og:title, og:description and og:image are present with absolute image URL.
twitter:card is present.

findings.title: No structured data (JSON-LD)
findings.detail: Structured data helps search engines show rich results (organisation, articles, products, breadcrumbs).

fix.summary: Add a JSON-LD block describing the page (Organization or WebSite on the home page, the right type elsewhere).
steps: Pick the schema.org type that matches the page.
Add a <script type="application/ld+json"> block.
Validate it with the Rich Results Test.
fix.codeHint: <script type="application/ld+json">{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"Organization","name":"Brand","url":"https://example.com/"}</script>
acceptance: The page has at least one valid JSON-LD block with an @type.

findings.title: No robots.txt
findings.detail: There's no robots.txt at the site root. Crawlers fall back to defaults and can't find your sitemap from it.

fix.summary: Add /robots.txt that allows crawling and links the sitemap.
steps: Create robots.txt at the site root.
Reference the sitemap URL in it.
fix.codeHint:
User-agent: *
Allow: /

Sitemap: https://example.com/sitemap.xml
acceptance: GET /robots.txt returns 200 with text/plain and a Sitemap line.

findings.title: No XML sitemap found
findings.detail: No sitemap was found at /sitemap.xml or in robots.txt. A sitemap helps search engines discover every page.

fix.summary: Publish /sitemap.xml listing your public pages and reference it in robots.txt.
steps: Generate a sitemap (most frameworks have a plugin).
Add a `Sitemap:` line to robots.txt.
Submit it in Google Search Console.
acceptance: /sitemap.xml (or the URL in robots.txt) returns valid XML listing the public pages.

findings.title: Page language is not set
findings.detail: The <html> element has no lang attribute, so screen readers may read the content with the wrong voice and pronunciation. Search engines also use it.

fix.summary: Add a lang attribute with the page language to the <html> element.
steps: Set lang on <html> in your root layout or template.
Use the right code per locale if the site is multilingual.
fix.codeHint: <html lang="en">
acceptance: <html> has a valid, non-empty lang attribute matching the content language.
fix.verify: In DevTools console: `document.documentElement.lang`

findings.title: Images without alt text
findings.detail: Images have no alt attribute. Screen readers announce the file name instead, and search engines get no description. (This also covers the SEO alt-text check.)

fix.summary: Give every meaningful image a short alt text describing it, and decorative images alt="".
steps: For each image, decide whether it conveys information.
Meaningful: add alt text that says what the image shows or does (not "image of").
Decorative: add alt="" so assistive tech skips it.
Images inside links: describe the link destination.
acceptance: Every has an alt attribute (empty for decorative images) or role="presentation".
Linked images have alt text describing the link.
fix.verify: In DevTools console: `document.querySelectorAll('img:not([alt])').length === 0`

findings.title: Form fields without labels
findings.detail: These inputs have no label. Placeholder text isn't a label: it disappears while typing and many screen readers ignore it.

fix.summary: Connect a visible <label> to each field with for/id, or wrap the field in the label.
steps: Add a <label for="field-id"> with clear text for each input, select and textarea.
Keep placeholders only as examples, not as the label.
If a visible label is impossible, use aria-label.
fix.codeHint:
<label for="email">Email address</label>
<input id="email" type="email" autocomplete="email">
acceptance: Every visible input, select and textarea has a programmatically associated label.

findings.title: No skip link
findings.detail: Keyboard users have to tab through the whole header and navigation on every page before reaching the content.

fix.summary: Add a "Skip to content" link as the first focusable element, visible on focus, pointing at the main content.
steps: Add the link as the first element inside <body>.
Give <main> an id and point the link at it.
Hide it off-screen until it receives focus.
fix.codeHint:
Skip to content …
.skip-link { position: absolute; left: -999px; } .skip-link:focus { left: 1rem; top: 1rem; }
acceptance: Pressing Tab once on page load focuses a visible "Skip to content" link.
Activating it moves focus to the main content.
fix.verify: Load the page, press Tab once, then Enter; focus should land on the main content.

findings.title: Keyboard focus is invisible
findings.detail: When these elements receive keyboard focus nothing visibly changes, so keyboard users lose track of where they are (WCAG 2.4.7).

fix.summary: Give every interactive element a clearly visible :focus-visible style, and never remove outlines without a replacement.
steps: Search the CSS for `outline: none` / `outline: 0` on :focus.
Add a :focus-visible rule with an outline of at least 2px in a colour with 3:1 contrast.
Check buttons, links and form fields by tabbing through the page.
acceptance: Every focusable element shows a visible focus indicator with at least 3:1 contrast against its surroundings.
fix.verify: Tab through the page; you should always see which element has focus.

findings.title: No main landmark
findings.detail: There's no <main> element. Screen reader users can't jump straight to the content, and skip links have nothing to target.

fix.summary: Wrap the primary content in a single <main> element, and use <header>, <nav> and <footer> for the rest.
steps: Wrap the page content (not header/footer) in <main id="main">.
Use <nav> for navigation blocks and <header>/<footer> for the page banner and footer.
fix.codeHint:
<header>…</header>
<main id="main">…</main>
<footer>…</footer>
acceptance: The page has exactly one <main> (or role="main").
Navigation is inside <nav>.

findings.title: Tap targets smaller than 24px
findings.detail: On a phone these controls are smaller than 24x24 CSS pixels, the WCAG 2.2 minimum (2.5.8), so people mis-tap.

fix.summary: Make each control at least 24x24px (44x44px is better) using padding, without changing the visual size of icons.
steps: Add padding or min-width/min-height to small links and buttons.
Increase spacing between adjacent small targets.
Recheck at a 390px-wide viewport.
acceptance: At 390px width, every tap target is at least 24x24 CSS px (or has 24px spacing to its neighbours).
fix.verify: DevTools device mode at 390px: hover each control and check its box size.

findings.title: Tap targets under 44px
findings.detail: These controls meet the 24px minimum but are smaller than the comfortable 44x44px recommended for touch.

fix.summary: Grow touch targets to 44x44px where the layout allows, using padding.
steps: Add padding to primary navigation, buttons and form controls until they reach 44px tall.
acceptance: Primary controls are at least 44x44 CSS px on mobile.

findings.title: Body text smaller than 16px
findings.detail: A large share of the running text is under 16px, which is hard to read on phones and for many older readers.

evidence.htmlSnippet: Beginner evenings every Thursday. Six weeks, all clay and firing included. Bring an apron and patience; we provide the rest.

fix.summary: Set body text to at least 16px (1rem) and size other text relative to it.
steps: Set `font-size: 1rem` (16px) or larger on body.
Use rem for paragraph and list text; keep smaller sizes for captions and legal text only.
fix.codeHint: body { font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.5; }
acceptance: Paragraph and list text renders at 16px or larger at all viewport widths.

findings.title: Lines of text are too long
findings.detail: Paragraph lines run past ~90 characters. Long lines make it hard to find the start of the next line.

evidence.htmlSnippet: Beginner evenings every Thursday. Six weeks, all clay and firing included. Bring an apron and patience; we provide the rest.

fix.summary: Limit text columns to about 60-75 characters with max-width.
steps: Add a max-width in ch units to prose containers.
fix.codeHint: .prose, article p { max-width: 68ch; }
acceptance: Paragraphs on a 1440px-wide screen have at most ~80 characters per line.

findings.title: Images without width and height
findings.detail: Images without width/height (or aspect-ratio) make the layout jump as they load (cumulative layout shift).

fix.summary: Add width and height attributes matching the intrinsic size, and let CSS scale them.
steps: Add width and height attributes to each (the intrinsic pixel size).
Keep `height: auto` in CSS so they stay responsive.
fix.codeHint: img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; }
acceptance: Every content has width and height attributes or a CSS aspect-ratio.

findings.title: No Content Security Policy
findings.detail: A Content-Security-Policy limits where scripts can load from, which blunts cross-site scripting.

fix.summary: Add a Content-Security-Policy header, starting in report-only mode.
steps: Start with `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` to see what would break.
List the script, style, image and font sources you need.
Switch to enforcing once reports are clean.
fix.codeHint: Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data: https:; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; frame-ancestors 'self'
acceptance: Responses include a Content-Security-Policy header (enforcing or report-only).

findings.title: No X-Content-Type-Options header
findings.detail: Without `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, browsers may guess file types, which can turn uploads into scripts.

fix.summary: Send `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` on all responses.
steps: Add the header in your host, CDN or server config.
fix.codeHint: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
acceptance: Responses include X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.

findings.title: No Referrer-Policy header
findings.detail: Without a Referrer-Policy, full URLs (which can include private query strings) may leak to other sites.

fix.summary: Send `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`.
steps: Add the header in your host, CDN or server config.
fix.codeHint: Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
acceptance: Responses include a Referrer-Policy header.

findings.title: Page can be framed by other sites
findings.detail: No X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors, so other sites can embed this page and trick visitors into clicking (clickjacking).

fix.summary: Send `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self'` (or X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN).
steps: Add the directive to your CSP, or add X-Frame-Options.
fix.codeHint:
Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self'
X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN
acceptance: Responses include frame-ancestors in CSP or X-Frame-Options.

findings.title: Near-duplicate colours
findings.detail: Several colours in use are almost identical. They usually come from one-off hex values instead of shared tokens, and make the palette feel slightly off.

fix.summary: Merge each near-duplicate pair into one token and replace the stray values.
steps: Pick the canonical value of each pair (the more common one).
Define it once as a CSS custom property.
Search the codebase for the other hex values and replace them with the variable.
fix.codeHint:
:root { --color-link: #1a5fb4; }
.a, .b, .c { color: var(--color-link); }
acceptance: No two colours in the extracted palette are within ΔE 6 of each other unless intentionally distinct.

findings.title: Too many font families
findings.detail: More than three typefaces are in use. It dilutes the brand and every web font adds download weight.

evidence.measured: 5 families: Georgia, Trebuchet MS, Verdana, Courier New, Arial

fix.summary: Reduce to two families (one for headings, one for body), plus a monospace if you show code.
steps: Pick the heading and body faces that best represent the brand.
Replace the others with those, using weights for hierarchy.
Remove unused @font-face rules and font links.
acceptance: At most 3 font families render on the page.

findings.title: Spacing is off-grid
findings.detail: Margins and paddings use arbitrary values instead of multiples of a base unit, so rhythm and alignment drift.

fix.summary: Adopt a 4px or 8px spacing scale as tokens and snap values to it.
steps: Define spacing tokens (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48…).
Replace odd values (7px, 13px, 19px) with the nearest token.
fix.codeHint: :root { --space-1: 4px; --space-2: 8px; --space-3: 16px; --space-4: 24px; --space-5: 32px; }
acceptance: At least 80% of margin, padding and gap values are multiples of 4px.

findings.title: Inconsistent corner radii
findings.detail: Many different border radii are in use, so cards, buttons and inputs look like they come from different systems.

fix.summary: Define 2-3 radius tokens (small, medium, pill) and use only those.
steps: Choose the radii you want to keep.
Replace the rest with the nearest token.
fix.codeHint: :root { --radius-sm: 4px; --radius-md: 8px; --radius-pill: 9999px; }
acceptance: At most 3 distinct non-zero border radii are used.

findings.title: No design tokens in CSS
findings.detail: No CSS custom properties were found on :root. Tokens make brand colours, type and spacing consistent and easy to change. (Informational; cross-origin stylesheets cannot be read.)

fix.summary: Move brand values into CSS custom properties. The brand tokens in this report are a ready-made starting point.
steps: Paste the generated :root block into your global stylesheet.
Replace hard-coded values with var(--…) references, component by component.
acceptance: :root defines colour, font, spacing and radius custom properties used by components.

findings.title: Text files sent without compression
findings.detail: HTML, CSS, JavaScript or SVG files are sent uncompressed. Gzip or Brotli typically cuts them by 70% or more.

fix.summary: Enable Brotli or gzip compression for text responses on the server or CDN.
steps: Turn on compression in the host/CDN settings, or in the web server (e.g. nginx `gzip on; brotli on;`).
Include text/html, text/css, application/javascript, image/svg+xml and application/json.
acceptance: Text responses over 1 KB are served with Content-Encoding: br or gzip.
fix.verify: Run `curl -sI -H "Accept-Encoding: br,gzip" <asset-url> | grep -i content-encoding`

findings.title: Large images in old formats
findings.detail: Large images are served as PNG or JPEG. WebP or AVIF are usually 30-60% smaller at the same quality.

fix.summary: Serve large images as AVIF or WebP (with a JPEG fallback if needed) and compress them.
steps: Convert the listed images (e.g. with Squoosh, sharp or your image CDN).
Use <picture> with type="image/avif" and "image/webp" sources, or an image component that negotiates formats.
acceptance: No image over 100 KB is served as PNG or JPEG.

findings.title: Largest Contentful Paint is slow
findings.detail: Largest Contentful Paint marks the time at which the largest text or image is painted. Learn more about the Largest Contentful Paint metric Measured by local Lighthouse (indicative lab data).

fix.summary: Make the largest above-the-fold element (usually the hero image or heading) render sooner.
steps: Identify the LCP element in DevTools > Performance (look for the LCP marker).
If it is an image: serve it in AVIF/WebP at display size, add fetchpriority="high", and never lazy-load it.
Preload the LCP image or font, and remove render-blocking CSS/JS in front of it.
Reduce server response time (cache HTML at the edge).
acceptance: Lighthouse mobile LCP is 2.5 s or less.
fix.verify: Run Lighthouse (mobile) in Chrome DevTools and read the LCP metric.

findings.title: Main thread is blocked by JavaScript
findings.detail: Sum of all time periods between FCP and Time to Interactive, when task length exceeded 50ms, expressed in milliseconds. Learn more about the Total Blocking Time metric. Measured by local Lighthouse (indicative lab data).

fix.summary: Ship less JavaScript up front and break long tasks into smaller ones.
steps: Find long tasks in DevTools > Performance.
Code-split routes and lazy-load heavy components.
Defer or remove third-party scripts.
Move expensive work off the main thread or yield with scheduler.yield/setTimeout.
acceptance: Lighthouse mobile TBT is 200 ms or less.
